\subsection{ArkLib's axiom baseline, and what is admitted at each pin}\label{sec:gen-lib-ark-baseline}

\paragraph{The baseline.} \file{scripts/}\allowbreak\file{axiom_baseline.json} at the old pin (dated 2026-09-08,
last changed by ArkLib \#887) is the output of ArkLib's \code{axiomsweep} tool
(\file{scripts/}\allowbreak\file{AxiomSweep.lean:8-60}): it walks the compiled environment of the whole library and
records every declaration whose statement or proof depends on \lean{sorryAx} (\enquote{the same
information as \texttt{\#print axioms}, for the whole library at once}). It is an allow-list: ArkLib's
CI runs \code{lake exe axiomsweep --check} (\file{.github/}\allowbreak\file{workflows/}\allowbreak\file{ci.yml:162-163}), which fails
when a tainted declaration is missing from the file and stays green when a listed one has since
been proved. The \code{build} check run of the pin commit concluded \code{success}. Hence a
declaration absent from the baseline is \lean{sorryAx}-free at the pin; one present may or may
not be. The baseline lists 291 declarations (\code{"sorry"}) and no non-standard axiom
(\code{"nonstandard": []}). Counted \lean{sorry} in code (non-comment lines) at the old pin:
\file{Security/Implications.lean} 9, \file{Append/Security.lean} 4, \file{General.lean} 2,
\file{Basic.lean} 1 (the \lean{numQueries} definition), \file{FiatShamir/Basic.lean} 1,
\file{LiftContext/Reduction.lean} 10, \file{Sumcheck/}\allowbreak\file{Spec/}\allowbreak\file{SingleRound.lean} 13,
\file{Component/SendWitness.lean} 1, \file{CapacityBounds.lean} 3; none in
\file{Security/Basic.lean}, \file{RoundByRound.lean}, \file{RbrGame.lean}, \file{Execution.lean},
\file{OracleInterface.lean}, \file{ProtocolSpec/*.lean},
\file{Append/{Basic,StateFunction,RoundByRound,Completeness,Execution}.lean},
\file{GuardedCompleteness.lean}, \file{GuardedNary.lean}, \file{OracleCompleteness.lean},
\file{CWSS/Guarded.lean}, \file{Commitments/}\allowbreak\file{Functional/}\allowbreak\file{Basic.lean},
\file{Component/{ReduceClaim,CheckClaim,RandomQuery,DoNothing}.lean},
\file{Sumcheck/Spec/General.lean}, \file{Domain.lean}, \file{Multilinear.lean},
\file{SchwartzZippelCounting.lean}. Whole library at the old pin: 192 code occurrences of
\lean{sorry} in 77 files.

\paragraph{At the new pin.} The baseline shrinks from 291 to 286 entries between the pins, but
among the declarations of the composition layer, the implications, the lifting, Fiat--Shamir and
the sumcheck specification \textbf{none was removed and none added} (the two baselines were
compared by name over the prefixes \lean{Verifier.}, \lean{OracleVerifier.}, \lean{Reduction.},
\lean{OracleReduction.}, \lean{Sumcheck.}, \lean{fiatShamir}, \lean{SendSingleWitness},
\lean{NoInteraction}, \lean{Extractor.}, \lean{CodingTheory.rs_mca}). Code-line \lean{sorry}
counts at the new pin: \file{Security/Implications.lean} 9 (unchanged), \file{Append/Security.lean}
4 (unchanged), \file{General.lean} 2, \file{FiatShamir/Basic.lean} 1,
\file{LiftContext/Reduction.lean} 10, \file{Sumcheck/}\allowbreak\file{Spec/}\allowbreak\file{SingleRound.lean} 13 (one fewer than the
old pin by the dossier's count; the leaves \lean{verifier_}\allowbreak\lean{rbrKnowledgeSoundness} and the lens
instances remain). \Cref{tab:gen-lib-ark-admitted} sets the blueprint's ledger of admissions
(\file{protocol-blueprint.md:257-267}) against both pins.

\subsection{The ported composition theorem}\label{sec:gen-lib-ark-port}

\paragraph{Provenance, verified.} \code{git show ca7a2577:ArkLib/OracleReduction/Composition/Sequential/Append/Knowledge.lean}
in the sibling ArkLib checkout (after \code{git fetch origin}; the commit is \enquote{style(ring-switching):
align names and streamline documentation}, 2026-09-09, head of pull request \#615,
\enquote{feat(ring-switching): add reusable packing proofs and protocol integrations}, author
alexanderlhicks) gives a 632-line file, saved as
\file{probes/}\allowbreak\file{lib-arklib/}\allowbreak\file{Knowledge_pr615_ca7a2577.lean.txt}. A \code{diff} against the local
587-line \file{LeanerVM/}\allowbreak\file{Protocol/}\allowbreak\file{ToArkLib/}\allowbreak\file{KnowledgeAppend.lean} shows exactly these differences
(the whole \code{diff} output was read):
\begin{enumerate}
\item Header: the local file adds its own title lines and keeps the ArkLib copyright, license and
  \enquote{Authors: ArkLib Contributors} lines.
\item The pull request's file is a classic Lean file (\code{import …}); the local one is a
  \code{module} with \code{public import} of the same two modules and an
  \code{@[expose] public section}. (The pull request predates ArkLib's move to the module system,
  which is the pin's own commit, \texttt{dca90385 feat(module-system): migrate to modules (\#897)};
  this is one reason the pull request is in conflict with \code{main}.)
\item The module docstring is rewritten (the pull request's says the same things: guarded first
  verifier, exact-object worst-case theorem, import it explicitly to avoid a cycle).
\item Everything is wrapped in \lean{namespace LeanerVM.}\allowbreak\lean{Protocol} (so the declarations are
  \lean{LeanerVM.}\allowbreak\lean{Protocol.}\allowbreak\lean{Verifier.}\allowbreak\lean{KnowledgeAppend.*},
  \lean{LeanerVM.}\allowbreak\lean{Protocol.}\allowbreak\lean{Verifier.}\allowbreak\lean{KnowledgeStateFunction.}\allowbreak\lean{appendGuarded},
  \lean{LeanerVM.}\allowbreak\lean{Protocol.}\allowbreak\lean{Verifier.}\allowbreak\lean{append_}\allowbreak\lean{rbrKnowledgeSoundnessWorstCaseWith_}\allowbreak\lean{of_guarded_}\allowbreak\lean{first}).
\item The two lemmas \lean{witness_left} and \lean{witness_right} (six and nine lines of proof in
  the pull request) are replaced by references to ArkLib's own
  \lean{Extractor.}\allowbreak\lean{wit_}\allowbreak\lean{mid_}\allowbreak\lean{append_}\allowbreak\lean{left} and \lean{wit_mid_append_right}
  (\file{Append/}\allowbreak\file{StateFunction.lean:51-71} at the pin), which are the same statements.
\item Docstrings are added to fourteen declarations that had none.
\item Two names are qualified (\lean{Verifier.}\allowbreak\lean{guarded_}\allowbreak\lean{accepting_}\allowbreak\lean{of_mem},
  \lean{Verifier.}\allowbreak\lean{append_}\allowbreak\lean{run_}\allowbreak\lean{guardedLeft}), as the namespace requires.
\item The four wrappers of the pull request are omitted: the averaged exact-object form
  (\lean{append_}\allowbreak\lean{rbrKnowledgeSoundnessWith_}\allowbreak\lean{of_worstCase_}\allowbreak\lean{of_guarded_}\allowbreak\lean{first}), the existential
  worst-case form (\lean{append_}\allowbreak\lean{rbrKnowledgeSoundnessWorstCase_}\allowbreak\lean{of_guarded_}\allowbreak\lean{first}), the existential
  averaged form (\lean{append_}\allowbreak\lean{rbrKnowledgeSoundness_}\allowbreak\lean{of_worstCase_}\allowbreak\lean{of_guarded_}\allowbreak\lean{first}) and the
  \lean{OracleVerifier} form.
\end{enumerate}
No proof step of the two main declarations differs. The blueprint's description (\enquote{verbatim
port \dots\ except that its two lemmas on the witness type reuse the pinned ArkLib's proofs; the
wrappers into the existential and averaged forms are left out}, file docstring \file{:31-37}) is
accurate. Both declarations depend on the three standard axioms (\cref{tab:gen-lib-ark-axioms}).

\paragraph{What the two declarations say.} \lean{Verifier.}\allowbreak\lean{KnowledgeStateFunction.}\allowbreak\lean{appendGuarded G K₁ K₂}
(\file{KnowledgeAppend.lean:474-488}) builds, from a guarded form \lean{G} of the first verifier
and knowledge state functions \lean{K₁} (for \lean{V₁}, relations \lean{R₁ → R₂}) and \lean{K₂}
(for \lean{V₂}, \lean{R₂ → R₃}), a knowledge state function of \lean{V₁.append V₂} for
\lean{R₁ → R₃} and for ArkLib's appended extractor \lean{E₁.append E₂ G.out}. Its state
(\lean{state}, \file{:182-196}) is: up to and including the seam, \lean{K₁} on the prefix; after
the seam, \enquote{the first check passes on the first half \textbf{and} \lean{K₂} on the second
half, at the statement the first verifier outputs (\lean{G.out s tr₁})}.
\begin{leancode}
extractors and knowledge states. The first round of the right component is included. -/
theorem append_rbrKnowledgeSoundnessWorstCaseWith_of_guarded_first (G : V₁.GuardedForm)
    (K₁ : V₁.KnowledgeStateFunction init impl R₁ R₂ E₁)
    (K₂ : V₂.KnowledgeStateFunction init impl R₂ R₃ E₂)
    {ε₁ : pSpec₁.ChallengeIdx → ℝ≥0} {ε₂ : pSpec₂.ChallengeIdx → ℝ≥0}
    (h₁ : V₁.rbrKnowledgeSoundnessWorstCaseWith init impl R₁ R₂ W₁ E₁ K₁ ε₁)
    (h₂ : V₂.rbrKnowledgeSoundnessWorstCaseWith init impl R₂ R₃ W₂ E₂ K₂ ε₂) :
    (V₁.append V₂).rbrKnowledgeSoundnessWorstCaseWith init impl R₁ R₃
      (Witness W₁ W₂) (E₁.append E₂ G.out) (KnowledgeStateFunction.appendGuarded G K₁ K₂)
      (Sum.elim ε₁ ε₂ ∘ ChallengeIdx.sumEquiv.symm) := by
  classical
\end{leancode}
\src{\file{LeanerVM/}\allowbreak\file{Protocol/}\allowbreak\file{ToArkLib/}\allowbreak\file{KnowledgeAppend.lean:508-518}, leanerVM \code{b435631}}

In words: if \lean{V₁} is worst-case round-by-round knowledge sound for \lean{(E₁, K₁)} at errors
\lean{ε₁} and \lean{V₂} for \lean{(E₂, K₂)} at errors \lean{ε₂}, then \lean{V₁.append V₂} is, for
the appended extractor and state function, at the error that assigns to each challenge \textbf{the
error of the component it belongs to} (\lean{Sum.}\allowbreak\lean{elim ε₁ ε₂ ∘ ChallengeIdx.}\allowbreak\lean{sumEquiv.}\allowbreak\lean{symm}). No
additive term appears: a bad transition of the composite at a challenge of the first component is
a bad transition of \lean{K₁} at the same prefix (\lean{state_left}, \lean{extractMid_left}); at a
challenge of the second component, including its first round where the seam extraction happens
(\lean{backward_right}, \lean{extractMid_seam}, \lean{left_related}), it is a bad transition of
\lean{K₂} at the prefix's second half and the statement \lean{G.out s tr₁}. Since \lean{h₂} is
quantified over all statements, it applies to that statement whatever \lean{tr₁} is. This is the
right error for round-by-round notions (each challenge keeps its own bound); the sum
$\sum \varepsilon$ only appears when passing to plain knowledge soundness
(\cref{sec:gen-lib-ark-implications}).

\paragraph{Hypotheses.} \lean{G : V₁.GuardedForm} (the first verifier is a Boolean check followed
by a deterministic verdict, \file{CWSS/Guarded.lean:112-118}) is the only hypothesis beyond the two
components' soundness; the second verifier is arbitrary; either component may have no round; the
shared oracle is arbitrary but the state functions and errors are for the same \lean{init},
\lean{impl}. The guarded form is \emph{data}: the composed extractor and state use \lean{G.out},
the first verifier's verdict function, to compute the statement handed to the second component.
On a rejected first half \lean{G.out} is whatever the form says (ArkLib's \lean{ofEmpty} uses a
fallback); it is used only under \lean{G.check = true} in the proofs, so this is harmless.

\paragraph{Is it a real restriction for leanVM's phases?} No. Over the empty shared oracle every
verifier is guarded: ArkLib proves \lean{Verifier.}\allowbreak\lean{GuardedForm.}\allowbreak\lean{ofEmpty}
(\file{Composition/}\allowbreak\file{Sequential/}\allowbreak\file{NoAmbient.lean:46-55} at the pin:
\lean{check := (V.}\allowbreak\lean{verify stmt tr).}\allowbreak\lean{run.}\allowbreak\lean{runEmpty.}\allowbreak\lean{isSome}, \lean{out := ….}\allowbreak\lean{getD (fallback stmt)}),
together with \lean{Prover.}\allowbreak\lean{instOutputIsPureEmpty} (\file{:39-43}). leanerVM's phases live over
\lean{[]ₒ} (\lean{Component.}\allowbreak\lean{Def.}\allowbreak\lean{red : OracleReduction []ₒ …}), and leanerVM supplies the guarded
forms by hand (\lean{PublicInput.guarded}, \lean{sendVerifierPure.}\allowbreak\lean{toGuardedForm}), which is more
readable but not necessary. It would be a restriction for a verifier that queries a shared oracle
(a random oracle): such a verifier is not guarded, and the compiled protocol's verifier (Merkle
paths hashed through the oracle) is of that kind; the blueprint composes only at the
oracle-protocol level, where none is.

\paragraph{The upstream, read on 2026-09-29 (read-only \code{gh}).} Pull request \#615 is
\textbf{open}, not a draft, \code{mergeable: CONFLICTING}, created 2026-07-07, last updated
2026-09-08, head \code{ca7a2577}. Its \file{Knowledge.lean} is not on ArkLib's \code{main}
(\file{Composition/}\allowbreak\file{Sequential/}\allowbreak\file{Append/} there has the same eleven files as the pin, no
\file{Knowledge.lean}); \file{Append/Security.lean} still admits \lean{append_soundness},
\lean{append_knowledgeSoundness}, \lean{append_rbrSoundness}, \lean{append_}\allowbreak\lean{rbrKnowledgeSoundness}
(four \lean{sorry}). Issue \#676 (\enquote{Sequential-composition and context-lifting layer is
stubbed, making composed security theorems vacuous}) is \textbf{open}, its body refreshed
2026-09-26. Its current scope says (verbatim):
\begin{quote}\small
This remains an open \textbf{legacy \lean{OracleReduction}} issue. \dots\ Generic legacy append
soundness, knowledge soundness, and round-by-round security still contain admissions in
\file{Composition/}\allowbreak\file{Sequential/}\allowbreak\file{Append/}\allowbreak\file{Security.lean}; derived wrappers inherit them. \dots\
\file{Security/Implications.lean} still have proof gaps. \dots\ Native Sumcheck (\#1214), shared
strategy execution (\#1216), and native composition (\#1218) are separate proved results. They do
not repair the axiom dependencies of legacy protocol clients. Use \#1 for the current interaction
framework and \#1222--\#1229 for the next composition work. Keep this issue open until its
remaining legacy claims are proved with correct assumptions or its consumers migrate with verified
correspondence. Do not assume an unrestricted stateful composition statement is provable merely
because its components are secure from the same fresh initialization.
\end{quote}
The last sentence is a warning that the admitted \lean{append_}\allowbreak\lean{rbrKnowledgeSoundness} (stateful
shared oracle, second component proved from a fresh \lean{init}) may be unprovable as stated;
leanerVM's port avoids the problem by requiring both components at the same \lean{init} and
\lean{impl} and, for completeness, the second from every deterministic state.

\paragraph{Consequence for the blueprint's plan.} The blueprint plans that \enquote{the port is
deleted, and its two names in \file{Component.lean} replaced by ArkLib's, when the pin moves past
\#615} (\file{:260}, \file{:1143-1144}, \file{:1429}). There is no evidence that \#615 will merge
in its current form (conflicting, pre-module, on a framework ArkLib now calls legacy,
\cref{sec:gen-lib-ark-legacy}). The condition should be stated as \enquote{when a revision of
ArkLib contains a proved guarded-first append for \lean{rbrKnowledgeSoundnessWorstCaseWith}},
whichever pull request brings it, and the plan should allow that this never happens on the legacy
framework (\cref{f:lib-legacy-framework}).

\subsection{What the new pin \texorpdfstring{\code{7653a901}}{7653a901} changes}\label{sec:gen-lib-ark-new}

The upgrade (\code{144c5aa}, \enquote{chore(deps): upgrade to Lean 4.34.1}) moves ArkLib from
\code{dca90385} to \code{7653a901}, 347 commits later (the revision the dossier had read as
\code{origin/main}), with VCVio \code{a4232d08}, CompPoly \code{572f9973} and Lean \code{v4.34.1}.
What follows was read in \file{.lake/packages/Arklib} at \code{7653a901}; the probes' outputs are
about the old pin and were not re-run.

\paragraph{The admitted theorems of the old pin are still admitted.} See
\cref{sec:gen-lib-ark-baseline} and \cref{tab:gen-lib-ark-admitted}. \lean{OracleVerifier.numQueries}
is still \lean{sorry} (\file{Basic.lean:505-507}), \lean{Commitment.extractability} still has
\lean{False} for its body (\file{Commitments/}\allowbreak\file{Functional/}\allowbreak\file{Basic.lean:249-254}),
\lean{fiatShamir_completeness} is still stated for the constant challenge oracle
(\file{FiatShamir/}\allowbreak\file{Basic.lean:163-173}).

\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{\lean{OracleReduction}}{OracleReduction} is now the \enquote{legacy}
framework, and the typed framework has no knowledge notion.}\label{sec:gen-lib-ark-legacy}
ArkLib's guide already called \file{ArkLib/OracleReduction/} \enquote{legacy IOR abstractions and
security theory} and \file{ArkLib/Interaction/} \enquote{typed interactions and dependent
reduction foundations} at the old pin (\file{AGENTS.md}, unchanged at \code{7653a901}). Between
the pins \file{ArkLib/Interaction/} grew from 7 to 28 files (+7280 lines) and
\file{ArkLib/}\allowbreak\file{ProofSystem/}\allowbreak\file{Sumcheck/}\allowbreak\file{Interaction/} was created (22 files, +3963 lines): the design
documents (\file{docs/design/05-roadmap.md}, dated 2026-09-26) say the composition milestones
\enquote{C1--C8 are merged} and \enquote{the immediate goal is to complete native Sumcheck:
computable messages and honest execution, round-by-round security, and precisely stated extraction
guarantees}. At \code{7653a901}:
\begin{itemize}
\item the typed framework proves \emph{plain} soundness and completeness of composed interactions
  and of native sumcheck (\file{Interaction/}\allowbreak\file{CompositionSoundness.lean}:
  \lean{run_appendFlat_soundness*}; \file{Sumcheck/}\allowbreak\file{Interaction/}\allowbreak\file{ProtocolSoundness.lean:201}
  \lean{execute_soundness}, \file{ProtocolCompleteness.lean:110}
  \lean{execute_}\allowbreak\lean{perfectCompleteness}), with no \lean{sorry} under \file{ArkLib/Interaction/} or
  \file{Sumcheck/Interaction/} per its status page;
\item it defines \textbf{no} knowledge soundness, no round-by-round notion and no extractor: a
  search for \code{knowledgeSound}, \code{rbrKnowledge}, \code{RoundByRound} and \code{extractor}
  in those two trees finds nothing;
\item issue \#676 (refreshed 2026-09-26) directs composition work to the typed framework and keeps
  the legacy admissions open \enquote{until its remaining legacy claims are proved with correct
  assumptions or its consumers migrate with verified correspondence}.
\end{itemize}
Consequences. (1) The spine's vocabulary (\lean{OracleReduction}, \lean{OracleVerifier.toVerifier},
\lean{KnowledgeStateFunction}, \lean{rbrKnowledgeSoundnessWorstCaseWith}, \lean{GuardedForm},
\lean{OracleReduction.append}, the guarded completeness theorems,
\lean{Verifier.}\allowbreak\lean{GuardedForm.}\allowbreak\lean{ofEmpty}) exists at the new pin with the same shapes (checked by name);
leanerVM's port compiled against it with proof-only edits. (2) Nothing in the typed framework can
replace the master theorems today: it has no notion of knowledge soundness. (3) The blueprint's
expectation that upstream will prove the legacy admissions (its ledger's \enquote{Action} column,
\file{docs/}\allowbreak\file{roadmap/}\allowbreak\file{protocol-blueprint.md:257-267}; \enquote{the port is deleted \dots\ when the pin
moves past \#615}) runs against upstream's stated direction, which is migration rather than repair
(\cref{f:lib-legacy-framework}). The status file's line \enquote{the spine stays on
\lean{OracleReduction}, whose security definitions the new executor does not yet carry}
(\file{protocol-status.md:201}) is the accurate description and should become the blueprint's.

\paragraph{The probability API.} VCVio at \code{a4232d08} introduces the notation
\lean{Pr{let x ← mx}[p x]} (\lean{prEvent}, \file{VCVio/}\allowbreak\file{EvalDist/}\allowbreak\file{ProbabilityNotation.lean:27}) and
keeps \lean{probEvent} with the lemma \lean{Pr{let x ← mx}[p x] = Pr[ p | mx]}
(\file{VCVio/}\allowbreak\file{EvalDist/}\allowbreak\file{Defs/}\allowbreak\file{Basic.lean:1102}), so the two spellings denote the same number. ArkLib
at \code{7653a901} restates every security definition in the new notation (the \code{diff} of
\file{Security/RoundByRound.lean} between the pins is the notation and the lemma names
\lean{probEvent_*} $\to$ \lean{prEvent_*}, \lean{OptionT.prEvent_mk_*}; the mathematical content
of \lean{KnowledgeStateFunction}, \lean{rbrKnowledgeSoundnessWorstCase(With)} and the two
implications is unchanged). leanerVM \code{144c5aa} follows:
\code{git diff b435631 144c5aa -- LeanerVM/Protocol} is 77 lines in, 76 out, confined to proofs and
notation (\file{GuardedVerdict.lean}, \file{UniformSample.lean}, \file{KnowledgeAppend.lean}:
\lean{Pr[P | c]} $\to$ \lean{Pr{let x ← c}[P x]}, \lean{if_pos}/\lean{dif_pos} $\to$
\lean{ite_eq_left}/\lean{dite_eq_left}, \lean{probEvent_mono} $\to$ \lean{prEvent_mono};
\file{PublicInput.lean} 10 lines, \file{Field.lean} 15 lines for CompPoly's new $\K$).
\file{docs/dependencies.md} at \code{144c5aa} says the bridges' \enquote{relations, extraction
conditions, and error bounds are retained} and asks to \enquote{review these statement changes
alongside the kernel audit, rather than relying on successful elaboration alone}. The statements
of the two theorems of \file{KnowledgeAppend.lean} differ from \code{b435631} only in the spelling
of the three probabilities they mention (\lean{state_full}'s hypothesis and the two \lean{calc}
blocks); the dossier read the diff and confirms no other change to a statement. The probes are
written in the old notation; at the new pin they would need the same mechanical rewriting before
they run (unverified: no Lean run is possible in the checkout).

\paragraph{The local port is still needed.} \file{Composition/}\allowbreak\file{Sequential/}\allowbreak\file{Append/} at
\code{7653a901} has the same eleven files as at \code{dca90385} and no \file{Knowledge.lean}; pull
request \#615 is open and conflicting. The local \file{KnowledgeAppend.lean} remains the only
proved guarded-first knowledge append, and \lean{Component.Security.append} depends on it at both
revisions.
